paper.title: Pure Exploration in Bandits with Linear Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration in bandits with linear constraints (fixed confidence)
unmapped: The answer is the optimal (possibly randomized) policy pi* = argmax_{pi in F} mu^T pi over a known polytope F = {pi in simplex: B pi <= c}
The learner knows the linear constraints (B, c)
Unique optimal policy assumption (Assumption 3), analogous to unique best arm
Rewards from a sub-Gaussian single-parameter exponential family (Assumption 1)
Exploration allocations restricted to a set Pi: Pi = simplex (end-of-time constraints) or Pi = F (anytime constraints, exploration must satisfy constraints in expectation)
settings.definition_quote: The learner has access to a non-empty and compact set of feasible policies F = {pi in Delta_{K-1}: B pi <= c} ... The goal of the learner is to recommend, with probability at least 1-delta, the unique optimal policy pi^*_{mu,F} ... Assumption 1: The reward of each arm is distributed according to a sub-Gaussian single-parameter exponential family ... Assumption 2: mu lies in a bounded domain D = [mu_min, mu_max]^K. Assumption 3: The optimal solution ... is unique.

settings.name_in_paper: Pure exploration with linear constraints, Gaussian arms with identical variance
unmapped: The answer is the optimal policy over a known polytope F = {pi in simplex: B pi <= c}
The learner knows the linear constraints (B, c)
Exploration allocations restricted to Pi (simplex or F)
settings.definition_quote: we consider the special case where all arms are Gaussian distributions with equal variance sigma^2.

symbols.T_F: constrained characteristic time: T_F(mu)^{-1} = sup_{w in Pi} inf_{lambda in Alt(mu)} sum_a w_a d(mu_a, lambda_a)

conditions: exploration allocations in Pi (simplex or F depending on scenario)

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: The stopping time $\tau$ of any $\delta$-PAC learner satisfy \begin{align} \E_{\bmu}[\tau] \geq \chartime(\bmu)\binaryKL{\delta}{1 - \delta}. \end{align}

results.notes: Also stated as Eq. (lb) in the main text. Proof follows Garivier & Kaufmann 2016.

symbols.d_max: max over neighbors pi' of pi* of d_{pi'}, the Euclidean distance from mu to the hyperplane lambda^T(pi* - pi') = 0 (so min_{pi'} 2 sigma^2/d_{pi'}^2 = 2 sigma^2/d_max^2)

conditions: Gaussian arms with identical variance sigma^2

source.label: prop:lb_lower_bound
source.quote: The characteristic time $\chartime(\bmu)$ satisfies the following bounds: \min_{\pol'} \frac{2\sigma^2}{d_{\pol'}^2} \leq \chartime(\bmu) \leq \min_{\pol'} \frac{2\sigma^2 K}{d_{\pol'}^2}. ... Corollary~\ref{prop:lb_lower_bound} implies a lower bound of \E[\tau] \geq \min_{\pol'} \frac{2\sigma^2}{d_{\pol'}^2} \binaryKL{\delta}{1-\delta}

results.notes: Recorded the implied sample-complexity lower bound stated right after Corollary 1, combined with Theorem 5. Corollary 1 itself bounds T_F between min 2sigma^2/d^2 and min 2sigma^2 K/d^2.

symbols.kappa: condition number (kappa^2 as in the paper) of a K x K matrix of linearly independent active constraints at pi*

conditions: Gaussian arms with identical variance sigma^2

source.label: prop:spectral
source.quote: Part (b): Let $\kappa^2$ be the condition number of a matrix $\hat{B}_{\optpol} \in \R^{K \times K}$ consisting of $K$ linearly independent active constraints at $\optpol$, then the sample complexity of any $\delta$-PAC learner is lower bounded as \E[\tau] = \Omega\left(\frac{H}{\kappa^2} \binaryKL{\delta}{1-\delta}\right) with $H = \frac{2\sigma^2}{\sum_{a\neq a^{*}} \Delta_a^2}$.

results.notes: Delta_a = mu_1 - mu_a. Appendix uses ||Delta||_2^2 and minimum condition number over such submatrices; part (a) gives an exact expression for T_F not recorded.

source.label: thm:ctns
source.quote: For any $\alpha > 1$ and $c(t, \delta)$ be defined as in Lemma~\ref{cor:stopping}, we have that the expected stopping time of CTnS satisfies \lim_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\E[\tau]}{\log \frac{1}{\delta}} \leq \chartime(\bmu), \, \forall \bmu \in \Domain.

results.notes: Proof actually concludes liminf E[tau]/log(1/delta) <= alpha T_F(mu) for all alpha>1; recorded as stated. Algorithm is delta-PAC by Lemma 2.

bound.expression_latex: \E[\tau] \leq T_0(\delta) + CK, T_0(\delta) := \max \left\{t \in \mathbb{N}: t \leq \chartime(\bmu)c(t, \delta) + O(\sqrt{tQ}) + O(\sqrt{t \log t}) \right\}

symbols.T_0: max{t in N: t <= T_F(mu) c(t,delta) + O(sqrt(tQ)) + O(sqrt(t log t))}
symbols.Q: upper bound on the losses fed to AdaGrad

tuning: f(t) = 3 log t + log log t
AdaGrad allocation player, best-response instance player

source.label: thm:cge
source.quote: The expected sample complexity of CGE satisfies $\E[\tau] \leq T_0(\delta) + CK,$ where $T_0(\delta) := \max \left\{t \in \mathbb{N}: t \leq \chartime(\bmu)c(t, \delta) + O(\sqrt{tQ}) + O(\sqrt{t \log t}) \right\}$. $C_\mu$ is problem-dependent constant, C is a universal constant and $Q$ is an upper bound on the losses provided to Adagrad.

results.notes: Implicit bound; implies asymptotic optimality. Compute deemed polynomial as CGE uses best-response projections (paper says computationally light), but not formally stated.
